partner_source.result_used: uniform all-rotation three-diffuse-bank density convergence for exact J, plus its pinned integrable Fresnel majorant

theorem: For independent normalized centered-unit-interval banks Y_j, arbitrary O in O(3), and exact active spectrum {a,b,-c}, a,b,c>=1, define S=a+b+c-3 and K_M(delta) as the supremum of the global output density norm over min bank size >=M and S>=delta. Then lim_{M->infinity} K_M(delta)=6/sqrt(2+delta). Hence K_M(0)->3sqrt(2), and every fully diffuse near-extremizer has a,b,c->1.
key_inequalities: spec_ne0(A_m)={1,1,-(1+1/m)} for explicit dense strict-slack family and ||p||_inf -> 3sqrt(2)
unresolved_next: Move outside the all-diffuse three-independent-bank chamber: bounded/intermediate bank sizes with non-aligned minority-sign geometry, rough cap-one laws, shared macroscopic rows/multiscale fragments, or additional active spectrum. Any proposed near-sharp proof should now exploit a quantified leverage/roughness alternative because fully diffuse spectral slack is rigidly subcritical.
